1 PASSED BY THE IV ADDL. DIST. JUDGE & MACT-XIII,
VIJAYAPUR IN MVC NO.868/2013 AND CONSEQUENTLY BE PLEASED TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION FROM Rs.2,25,000/- TO Rs.10,00,000/- WITH INTEREST @ 12%
PER ANNUM FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ACTUAL REALIZATION BY FASTENING THE LIABILITY ON RESPONDENT NO.2 INSURANCE COMPANY, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 THIS MFA HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 13.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT

This is petitioner's appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act ('M.V.Act' for short),
challenging the impugned judgment and award, by which though the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.4,50,000/-, it disallowed 50% of the compensation on the ground that petitioner contributed toward the cause of the accident.

It has also absolved respondent No.2/Insurance company on the ground that petitioner was a gratuitous passenger and at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license.
2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that on 16.04.2013 at 9.00 a.m., he and others were traveling in Cruiser Jeep bearing registration No.KA-28/M-9859 ('offending vehicle' for short) from Tikota to Dhulkhed.
When they were near Ballolli village, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in rash or negligent manner and tried to over take a vehicle ahead of it without taking proper precaution.
As a result of the same, petitioner sustained injury to his left hand including fracture.
Despite prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
On account of the injuries, he is unable to work as he used to prior to the accident.

As owner and insurer of the offending vehicle,
respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Though respondent No.1 appeared through counsel, he has not filed written statement.

5. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement disputing the age, occupation and income of the petitioner and that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, petitioner had kept his left hand outside the window and thereby contributed towards the cause of the accident.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license.

Since it is a private vehicle and as the driver of the offending vehicle had allowed the passengers to be carried in the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

2 7.

In support of his case, petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P1 to 13.
8.
On behalf of respondent No.2, one witness is examined as RW-1 and Ex.R1 and 2 are marked.
9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.4,50,000/-.

However, by holding that petitioner has contributed 50%
negligence towards the cause of accident, it has disallowed 50% of the compensation, on the ground that at the time accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license and since gratuitous passengers were carried in the offending vehicle, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and on this ground it has absolved respondent No.2 from paying the compensation and directed respondent No.1/owner to pay the same.
The details of the compensation granted by the Tribunal is as detailed below:

Heads Amount  In Rs.
 Medical expenses 2,25,000  Pain and sufferings 1,00,000  Loss of amenities 75,000  Attendant charges 30,000  Loss of income during treatment 20,000  period
During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the impugned judgment and award is against the well established principles of law.
The compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has erred in holding that petitioner has contributed 50% negligence towards cause of accident and thereby disallowed 50% of the compensation.

The Tribunal has erred in holding that there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and thereby absolving respondent No.2/Insurance company from paying the compensation and prays to allow the appeal, enhance the compensation and direct respondent No.2 to pay the entire compensation.
11. On the other hand, learned counsel representing respondent No.2/Insurance Company submitted that admittedly the offending vehicle is a private vehicle covered by a private policy.
The evidence placed on record indicate that gratuitous passengers were being transported in the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.

The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license and for these reasons and also the reason that petitioner has contributed towards the cause of accident, the Tribunal is justified in disallowing 50% of the compensation and absolving respondent No.2 from paying the compensation and prays to dismiss the appeal.

12. Heard arguments and perused the record.

3 13.

Having regard to the specific contentions raised in the appeal, at the outset it is necessary to examine whether petitioner is responsible for the cause of accident and contributed towards the same and whether the Tribunal is justified in disallowing 50% of the compensation on that ground.

As evident from the complaint averments and other material placed on record, including the testimony of petitioner who is examined as PW-1, undisputedly the offending vehicle is a private vehicle i.e., it is not a commercial vehicle meant to carry the passengers.
As admitted by PW-1, at the time of accident, about 20-25 persons were traveling in the offending vehicle, though its seating capacity is 12.
In fact during his cross-examination, PW-1 has specifically stated that a sum of Rs.1,700/- was paid towards fare and agent was taking them to the vine and grapes garden for harvesting grapes.

This piece of evidence establish beyond reasonable doubt though the offending vehicle is a private vehicle, it was being used for transporting gratuitous passengers on payment of fare.
14.

Though respondent No.2 has taken up a specific defence that at the time of accident driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license, it has not lead any evidence to show that attempts were made to ascertain whether he was holding a valid driving license or not.
However, it is proved that there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, by transporting passengers.
15. Now the next question is whether the petitioner has contributed towards the cause of accident.
The evidence placed on record indicate that at the time of accident, petitioner was sitting on the left seat by the side of the driver in front row.
Evidence placed on record indicated that he had put his left hand outside the window to signal that driver is over taking the vehicle.

However, from the material placed on record it is evident that the driver of the offending vehicle tried to over take a vehicle which is proceeding before it without taking proper care and observing the on coming vehicle from the opposite direction.
On sighting the vehicle coming from the opposite direction, he has failed to reduce its speed and take it to the left side.
On the other hand, suddenly he has tried to pass the offending vehicle through two vehicles i.e., one which was going ahead of him and one which was coming from opposite side.
On account of his sudden action, it appears petitioner could not withdraw his hand immediately and in the process, his hand brushed against the vehicle which was proceeding ahead.
As a result petitioner sustained injury to his left hand.
16. It is not the case of respondent No.1 that despite directions, petitioner was keeping his hand outside the window without any reason.

On the other hand, it is specifically deposed by petitioner that he had put his left hand outside the left window only to give an indication i.e., signal to the vehicle ahead of them that the offending vehicle is over taking it.
From the proper appreciation of the material placed on record, it is proved that there was no negligence or contribution on the part of petitioner in the cause of the accident.

On account of sudden move made by the driver of the offending vehicle, he did not have the time to withdraw his hand and consequently, it was caught between the offending vehicle and the vehicle on the left side.
In the circumstances, the Tribunal is not justified in holding that the petitioner had contributed towards the cause of the accident and quantifying the same at 50%.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled for entire compensation without any deduction towards contributory negligence.

Santosh vs Babusab And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190559803/
4 17.
Now coming to the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal.

Though the material placed on record by the petitioner prove that he suffered compound type III-B comminuted shattered fracture left humorous without DNVD and it is grievous in nature, however, he has not examined the doctor and there is no disability certificate.
Thus, petitioner has not proved that he has suffered any disability.

Taking into consideration the nature of injury suffered, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering, Rs.75,000/-
under the head loss of amenities, Rs.30,000/- under the attendant charges and Rs.20,000/- under the head loss of income during treatment period.
Similarly, based on the medical bills it has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,25,000/- under the head medical expenses.

Having regard to the nature of the injury suffered and the evidence placed on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that the compensation granted is just and reasonable and it requires no interference by this Court.
18. Now, coming to the question of liability.

Having regard to the fact that in a private vehicle,
passengers were being transported on hire basis, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, therefore respondent No.2/Insurance company is absolved from paying the compensation.

However, in the light of the decision reported in New India Assurance Co.Ltd, Bijapur by its Divisional Manager Vs. Yallavva & Anr1, which was also a case where claimant was traveling in a goods vehicle and his risk was not compulsorily covered under Section 147 and also in the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu and Ors. Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is a fit case to direct respondent No.2 to pay the compensation and recover the same from respondent No.1 and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ( ii) The total compensation quantified by the Tribunal at Rs.4,50,000/- is confirmed.
However, the findings of the Tribunal that ILR 2020 KAR 2239 petitioner contributed towards the cause of accident is set aside.

(iii) Respondent No.2 is directed to pay a total sum of Rs.4,50,000/- together with interest at 6%
p.a. to the petitioner within a period of six weeks from the date of this order and recover the same from respondent No.1.
(iv) The Registry is directed to send back the trial Court records along with copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
Sd/-
